[MATH: [4; − 1; 3]]

[MATH: [4; − 1; 3]]

If [MATH: x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,] then what is [MATH: x_1+x_2?]

sections.normalized_html:
If [MATH: x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,] then we have

[MATH: x_{1}[4; − 1; 3] + x_{2}[1; 0; 1]|= [5; − 5; 0]; [4x_{1} + x_{2}; − x_{1}; 3x_{1} + x_{2}]|= [5; − 5; 0].]

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

[MATH: {4x_{1} + x_{2} = 5; − x_{1} = − 5; 3x_{1} + x_{2} = 0]

From the second equation, we obtain [MATH: x_1=5,] which we substitute into the first equation to get

[MATH: 4x_{1} + x_{2}|= 5; 4(5) + x_{2}|= 5; x_{2}|= − 15.]

Finally, we substitute [MATH: x_1=5] and [MATH: x_2=-15] into the third equation to get

[MATH: 3x_{1} + x_{2}|= 0; 3(5) + (− 15)|= 0; 0|= 0,]

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is [MATH: x_1=5] and [MATH: x_2=-15,] which means

[MATH: 5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.]

Consequently,

[MATH: x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.]

Consider the vectors

If [MATH: x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,] then what is [MATH: x_1+x_2+x_3?]
sections.readable_text:
Consider the vectors

[MATH: [0; 1; 0]]

If [MATH: x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,] then what is [MATH: x_1+x_2+x_3?]

sections.normalized_html:
Since [MATH: \mathbf{b}] is a linear combination of vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}] and [MATH: \mathbf{a_3}] with coefficients [MATH: x_1,\, x_2] and [MATH: x_3,] respectively, we have [MATH: x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2} + x_{3}a_{3}|= b; x_{1}[0; 1; 0] + x_{2}[1; 0; − 1] + x_{3}[1; 2; 3]|= [1; 1; 7]; [0; x_{1}; 0] + [x_{2}; 0; − x_{2}] + [x_{3}; 2x_{3}; 3x_{3}]|= [1; 1; 7]; [x_{2} + x_{3}; x_{1} + 2x_{3}; − x_{2} + 3x_{3}]|= [1; 1; 7].]

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

[MATH: {x_{2} + x_{3} = 1; x_{1} + 2x_{3} = 1; − x_{2} + 3x_{3} = 7]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

[MATH: 0|1|1|1; 1|0|2|1; 0|− 1|3|7]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

[MATH: M|= [0|1|1|1; 1|0|2|1; 0|− 1|3|7]|R_{1}|↔R_{2}; ∼[1|0|2|1; 0|1|1|1; 0|− 1|3|7]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} + R_{2}; ∼[1|0|2|1; 0|1|1|1; 0|0|4|8]|R_{3}|:=(1)/(4)R_{3}; ∼[1|0|2|1; 0|1|1|1; 0|0|1|2].]

The system is now [MATH: {x_{1} + 2x_{3} = 1; x_{2} + x_{3} = 1; x_{3} = 2.]

From the third equation, we get [MATH: x_3 = 2.] Substituting this into the second equation, we get [MATH: x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,] and substituting [MATH: x_3=2] into the first equation, we get [MATH: x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.]

So the solution of the system is [MATH: x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,] which means

[MATH: -3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.]

Consequently,

[MATH: x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Consider a vector [MATH: \mathbf{u}] which is given in terms of the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{v_1}] and [MATH: \mathbf{v_2}] as follows:
[MATH: {\color{red}3}{\color{blue}\mathbf{v_1}}+({\color{red}-2}){\color{blue}\mathbf{v_2}} = \mathbf{u}]

Content:
Here, we say that [MATH: \mathbf{u}] is a linear combination of the vectors [MATH: {\color{blue}\mathbf{v_1}}] and [MATH: {\color{blue}\mathbf{v_2}}] with coefficients [MATH: {\color{red}3}] and [MATH: {\color{red}-2}] respectively.

Content:
In general, a linear combination of [MATH: n] vectors [MATH: \mathbf{v_1},\mathbf{v_2},\dots,\mathbf{v_n}] is the weighted sum
[MATH: {\color{red}x_1}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_1}+{\color{red}x_2}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2}+\cdots + {\color{red}x_n}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_n} = \mathbf{u},]
where [MATH: {\color{red}x_1},{\color{red}x_2},\dots,{\color{red}x_n}\in\mathbb{R}.] We say that [MATH: \mathbf{u}] is a linear combination of the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{\color{blue}v_1},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2},\dots,\mathbf{\color{blue}v_n}] with coefficients (or weights) [MATH: {\color{red}x_1},{\color{red}x_2},\dots,{\color{red}x_n},] respectively.

Content:
For instance,
[MATH: [1; − 1]]
is the linear combination of vectors [MATH: \mathbf{\color{blue}v_1},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_3}] with coefficients [MATH: {\color{red}2}, {\color{red}0}, {\color{red}\dfrac{1}{2}},] respectively.

Item 8 — Example: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
If [MATH: x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2 = \mathbf d,] then we have

[MATH: x_{1}[4; − 1; 3] + x_{2}[1; 0; 1]|= [5; − 5; 0]; [4x_{1} + x_{2}; − x_{1}; 3x_{1} + x_{2}]|= [5; − 5; 0].]

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

[MATH: {4x_{1} + x_{2} = 5; − x_{1} = − 5; 3x_{1} + x_{2} = 0]

From the second equation, we obtain [MATH: x_1=5,] which we substitute into the first equation to get

[MATH: 4x_{1} + x_{2}|= 5; 4(5) + x_{2}|= 5; x_{2}|= − 15.]

Finally, we substitute [MATH: x_1=5] and [MATH: x_2=-15] into the third equation to get

[MATH: 3x_{1} + x_{2}|= 0; 3(5) + (− 15)|= 0; 0|= 0,]

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is [MATH: x_1=5] and [MATH: x_2=-15,] which means

[MATH: 5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.]

Consequently,

[MATH: x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.]

Item 11 — Example: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

Example Prompt:
Consider the vectors

[MATH: [0; 1; 0]]

If [MATH: x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,] then what is [MATH: x_1+x_2+x_3?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Since [MATH: \mathbf{b}] is a linear combination of vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}] and [MATH: \mathbf{a_3}] with coefficients [MATH: x_1,\, x_2] and [MATH: x_3,] respectively, we have
[MATH: x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2} + x_{3}a_{3}|= b; x_{1}[0; 1; 0] + x_{2}[1; 0; − 1] + x_{3}[1; 2; 3]|= [1; 1; 7]; [0; x_{1}; 0] + [x_{2}; 0; − x_{2}] + [x_{3}; 2x_{3}; 3x_{3}]|= [1; 1; 7]; [x_{2} + x_{3}; x_{1} + 2x_{3}; − x_{2} + 3x_{3}]|= [1; 1; 7].]

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

[MATH: {x_{2} + x_{3} = 1; x_{1} + 2x_{3} = 1; − x_{2} + 3x_{3} = 7]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

[MATH: 0|1|1|1; 1|0|2|1; 0|− 1|3|7]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

[MATH: M|= [0|1|1|1; 1|0|2|1; 0|− 1|3|7]|R_{1}|↔R_{2}; ∼[1|0|2|1; 0|1|1|1; 0|− 1|3|7]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} + R_{2}; ∼[1|0|2|1; 0|1|1|1; 0|0|4|8]|R_{3}|:=(1)/(4)R_{3}; ∼[1|0|2|1; 0|1|1|1; 0|0|1|2].]

The system is now
[MATH: {x_{1} + 2x_{3} = 1; x_{2} + x_{3} = 1; x_{3} = 2.]

From the third equation, we get [MATH: x_3 = 2.] Substituting this into the second equation, we get
[MATH: x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,]
and substituting [MATH: x_3=2] into the first equation, we get
[MATH: x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.]

So the solution of the system is [MATH: x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,] which means

[MATH: -3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.]

Consequently,

[MATH: x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.]
